See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information. 18 19 ### Next.js Version 20 21 To update to Next.js version 13, run the following command using your preferred package manager: 22 23 ```bash package="pnpm" 24 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 25 ``` 26 27 ```bash package="npm" 28 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 29 ``` 30 31 ```bash package="yarn" 32 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 33 ``` 34 35 ```bash package="bun" 36 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 37 ``` 38 39 ### ESLint Version 40 41 If you're using ESLint, you need to upgrade your ESLint version: 42 43 ```bash package="pnpm" 44 pnpm add -D eslint-config-next@latest 45 ``` 46 47 ```bash package="npm" 48 npm install -D eslint-config-next@latest 49 ``` 50 51 ```bash package="yarn" 52 yarn add -D eslint-config-next@latest 53 ``` 54 55 ```bash package="bun" 56 bun add -D eslint-config-next@latest 57 ``` 58 59 > **Good to know**: You may need to restart the ESLint server in VS Code for the ESLint changes to take effect. Open the Command Palette (`cmd+shift+p` on Mac; `ctrl+shift+p` on Windows) and search for `ESLint: Restart ESLint Server`. 60 61 ## Next Steps 62 63 After you've updated, see the following sections for next steps: 64 65 - [Upgrade new features](#upgrading-new-features): A guide to help you upgrade to new features such as the improved Image and Link Components. 66 - [Migrate from the `pages` to `app` directory](#migrating-from-pages-to-app): A step-by-step guide to help you incrementally migrate from the `pages` to the `app` directory. 67 68 ## Upgrading New Features 69 70 Next.js 13 introduced the new [App Router](/docs/app) with new features and conventions. The new Router is available in the `app` directory and co-exists with the `pages` directory. 71 72 Upgrading to Next.js 13 does **not** require using the App Router. You can continue using `pages` with new features that work in both directories, such as the updated [Image component](#image-component), [Link component](#link-component), [Script component](#script-component), and [Font optimization](#font-optimization). 73 74 ### `` Component 75 76 Next.js 12 introduced new improvements to the Image Component with a temporary import: `next/future/image`. These improvements included less client-side JavaScript, easier ways to extend and style images, better accessibility, and native browser lazy loading. 77 78 In version 13, this new behavior is now the default for `next/image`. 79 80 There are two codemods to help you migrate to the new Image Component: 81 82 - [**`next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-to-legacy-image): Safely and automatically renames `next/image` imports to `next/legacy/image`. Existing components will maintain the same behavior. 83 - [**`next-image-experimental` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-experimental): Dangerously adds inline styles and removes unused props. This will change the behavior of existing components to match the new defaults. To use this codemod, you need to run the `next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod first. 84 85 ### `` Component 86 87 The [`` Component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) no longer requires manually adding an `` tag as a child. This behavior was added as an experimental option in [version 12.2](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-12-2) and is now the default. Everything from the Pages Router is now in the App Router, written in TypeScript, and the `pages/` directory is deleted. `next build` and `tsc --noEmit` both pass. I also ran `next start` and requested every route to check the status codes, titles, meta tags and all the API methods.

**File mapping**

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `_app.js` + `_document.js` | `app/layout.tsx`: the root layout with the header, nav and footer. Head tags moved to the `metadata` export. The Google Fonts `<link>`s became `next/font/google` (Inter, weights 400/500/600). |
| `index.js` (`getServerSideProps`) | `app/page.tsx`: an async Server Component. `req.headers` became `await headers()`, and the fetch uses `cache: 'no-store'`. |
| `blog/index.js` (ISR 60s) | `app/blog/page.tsx` with `export const revalidate = 60`. |
| `blog/[id].js` | `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx`: `getStaticPaths` became `generateStaticParams`, `fallback: 'blocking'` became `dynamicParams = true`, and `revalidate: 300` is kept. `notFound: true` became `notFound()`, and `<Head>` became `generateMetadata`. |
| `404.js` | `app/not-found.tsx` |
| `_error.js` | `app/error.tsx`, plus `app/global-error.tsx` for errors in the root layout. Both use the `retry` prop. |
| `api/posts/*.js` | `app/api/posts/route.ts` and `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts`. Each method is its own exported function using `Response.json`. |

**Replaced APIs and new files**
- **`useRouter` from `next/router`:** replaced by the one from `next/navigation`. It's only used inside two small client components, `PushButton` and `BackButton` in `components/NavigationButtons.tsx`, so the pages themselves stay Server Components. Internal `<a href>` links are now `<Link>`.
- **`router.isFallback`:** removed with no replacement. It was never true under `fallback: 'blocking'`. I briefly tried a `loading.tsx`, but it made unknown post IDs return status 200 instead of 404, so I took it out.
- **Manual 405 handling:** dropped, because Route Handlers return 405 automatically for methods that aren't exported. I checked: `PATCH` gets 405, and `OPTIONS` lists the allowed methods.
- **`AppProvider`:** now a typed client component (`'use client'`) with a `Theme` type.
- **Types and fetching:** new `lib/posts.ts` holds the `Post` and `Comment` types and the fetch helpers.
- **Global CSS:** moved to `app/globals.css`.

**Behaviour changes**
- The fetch helpers now check `res.ok`. Before, an unknown post ID crashed the page; now it shows the 404 page with a real 404 status.
- The two API routes that read a request body (`POST /api/posts` and `PUT /api/posts/[id]`) now treat an unreadable body as empty instead of throwing. `POST` still returns 400 when title or content is missing.
- The page titles are the same as before. The `_error` page no longer shows "error occurred on server/client" text, because `error.tsx` doesn't receive a status code.
- The layout still points the favicon at `/favicon.ico`, as before, but there's no `public/` folder in the repo, so that request 404s just as it did originally.

**Other changes**
- `next build` added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to the `include` list in `tsconfig.json` and reformatted the file.
- I added `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts` and `*.tsbuildinfo` to `.gitignore`.
- Nothing is committed.
